ZOMATO.why: Profit turned after years of losses: Q4 FY26 consolidated profit was ₹174 crore on revenue of ₹17,290 crore, helped by a recovering food delivery business and Blinkit's quick commerce arm moving toward profit. The July 2026 rally followed Q1 FY27 results: food delivery order value grew 20% year on year, and tight inventory control cut working-capital needs. The stock rose about 34% from its March low.
ZOMATO.outlook: Management targets 5-6% margins over time and $1 billion of adjusted EBITDA by FY29, and expects Blinkit order value to compound near 60% a year for three years. 27 of 29 analysts rate it Buy; the highest post-Q1 target found was ₹506 (CLSA). Risk: quick commerce competition and the profit base is still thin.

EASEMYTRIP.why: The stock has fallen far below its IPO price (shown here adjusted for splits and bonuses). Revenue slipped to ₹573 crore in FY26 from ₹603 crore, with a net loss of ₹48 crore in FY26 (₹109 crore in FY25). Reports cite share-of-flights pressure from rivals such as ixigo, a push into EV buses, venture funds and medical tourism, block sales by the promoter, and an ED search tied to the Mahadev betting case.
EASEMYTRIP.outlook: No 2026 management guidance or turnaround plan turned up. The latest data shows falling revenue and continued losses, so the outlook rests on whether the airline ticketing business stabilises. Treat as high risk until quarterly results show a clear turn.

NAZARA.why: FY26 revenue rose 13% to ₹1,829 crore and EBITDA jumped 66% to ₹255 crore, with over 90% of gaming revenue earned overseas. But the 2025 law banning real-money gaming forced a ₹914.7 crore write-down on its PokerBaazi parent stake (Moonshine), which is why the stock is only modestly above its IPO price despite the operating gains.
NAZARA.outlook: Growth now comes from acquisitions: a $100.3 million deal for Spanish platforms Bluetile and BestPlay in March 2026, funded by preferential issues (₹500 crore and a planned ₹733.5 crore). Choice Institutional had a Buy and ₹390 target in late 2025. No post-ban Moonshine outlook was found. Risks: acquisition integration and dilution.

CARTRADE.why: FY26 profit rose 68% to ₹243.5 crore and EBITDA margin widened to about 33% from 24%; the shares jumped over 15% on the results day in May 2026 and rallied about 23.5% over four sessions in June. Drivers cited: an AI initiative announced in February 2026 aimed at lifting margins, and OLX India's Elite Buyer programme passing 80,000 sign-ups in May 2026.
CARTRADE.outlook: Management's stated path is growth through AI features, monetisation and margin expansion. No analyst targets were found. Valuation is already high (price-to-earnings above 50 in February), which leaves less room for a miss.

NYKAA.why: Growth is broad: the provisional Q2 FY27 update showed GMV growth near 30% and net revenue growth in the late twenties, with fashion (NSV up in the late forties) now growing faster than beauty (late twenties). The shares are up about 63% over the 12 months to January 2026. Q2 FY26 profit rose 3.4x to ₹34.43 crore but missed estimates. (Price shown is adjusted for the 2025 bonus issue.)
NYKAA.outlook: Morgan Stanley is Overweight with a ₹356 target (about 10% upside); HDFC Securities is Sell at ₹200, calling fashion a work in progress and doubting beauty margins. FY27 margin and profit figures were not found. Valuation is rich, which caps upside unless growth turns into margins.

FINO.why: Listed below its ₹577 issue price and fell sharply in March 2026, hitting an all-time low near ₹113.55 after a GST-intelligence probe: a person named in the report was arrested on 27 February under GST law, and the bank said it has no role in the programme managers' operations. Analysts also expected FY26 revenue to dip about 2.9% and earnings per share to fall 15%.
FINO.outlook: Deposit balances reached about ₹2,900 crore in March 2026, up nearly 9% in two weeks, and about 1.5 lakh new accounts were added after 27 February. No outlook beyond March was found, so the probe's outcome is the main swing factor.

POLICYBZR.why: Insurance premiums sold on the platform grew 42% to ₹29,934 crore in FY26; new protection premiums (health and term) rose 67%, and lending disbursals rose 50% to ₹30,740 crore. Profit after tax excluding exceptional items rose 115% to ₹670 crore, and renewal and trail revenue grew 40% to ₹935 crore.
POLICYBZR.outlook: Elara initiated Buy with a ₹1,990 target (about 23% upside), expecting a 33% revenue CAGR and 51% profit CAGR over FY26-29. The stock had slipped about 15% over six months to near ₹1,624 in June 2026. Main risk: insurers cutting intermediary payouts; valuation is also demanding.

PAYTM.why: Paytm posted its first full-year profit: ₹552 crore for FY26 against a ₹663 crore loss the year before, on revenue up 22.2% to ₹8,437 crore, credited to AI-led cost discipline and operating leverage. The RBI cancelled Paytm Payments Bank's licence from 24 April 2026, but the company says it has no material exposure to it.
PAYTM.outlook: Management says it will not seek an NBFC licence and will keep a partner-led lending model. Goldman Sachs expects EBITDA to compound over 50% a year to 2030, and Citi and Bernstein are positive; Motilal Oswal is Neutral with targets near ₹1,300, so much of the recovery may be priced in.

LATENTVIEW.why: FY26 revenue grew about 20% to over ₹1,000 crore, with AI work making up 49% of operations. Financial services grew over 80%, and 72% of revenue comes from clients of over five years. The share price has still fallen about 41% over the past year as a top technology client consolidated vendors and insourced work.
LATENTVIEW.outlook: FY27 guidance is slower: revenue growth of 12-13% with a 21-22% EBITDA margin. PL Capital estimates a $6.5-7 million annual revenue hit from the lost client, with 50-60% expected to be recovered through AI-led wins. AI and partnership spending is pressing margins in the near term.

RATEGAIN.why: The stock rose about 83% from April to a June 2026 high of ₹801.8, driven by the $250 million Sojern acquisition, a strong Q4 FY26 and institutional buying. Margins have weakened (Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 18.2% against 21.7%), and net debt was about ₹722 crore in March 2026.
RATEGAIN.outlook: Management guides to roughly 55-60% revenue growth including Sojern, with a long-term ambition of $1 billion revenue by FY30-31, and expects acquisition debt cleared by FY28. Analysts are split: a bearish case at ₹450 against bullish targets of ₹875. At around 49x earnings the price reflects execution, not current profit.
